Title: rexecute (
Description:
This function can be used to execute SQL on a remote data source
    directly.
The result_set parameter is useful for
	obtaining a result-set quickly and easily. However, if the result-set is
	going to be large, this comes at a cost in terms of time and resources,
	particularly memory, since Virtuoso will have to obtain all results from
	the statement and build the result-set arrays in memory before returning
	back to the caller.
result_set
A more efficient way is to obtain a cursor handle and iterate
    through the result set one row at a time:
rexecute()
rnext()
rmoreresults()
SQL_NO_DATA_FOUND
rnext()
rclose()
To keep Virtuoso from obtaining the whole result set from the
    remote, pass NULL as the result_set parameter
    when calling rexecute.
result_set
Rexecute() supports IN parameters and can also
    support INOUT and OUT parameters. If INOUT and OUT parameters are to be used
    then cursors should not be used with this function (as the values of output
    parameters in ODBC are not guaranteed to be set before SQLMoreResults()
    returns SQL_NO_DATA_FOUND). Rexecute supports INOUT and
    OUT parameters by extending the in_params vector
	and requiring it to be a PL variable so values can be set back to it.
Rexecute()
Rexecute
in_params
Unless explicitly granted, only the DBA group is permitted to use the rexecute() to maintain security. Caution is required
	here since any user granted use of rexecute() has
	full control of the remote data source set-up by the DBA, however limited
	to the overall abilities of the remote user on the remote data source.
	Users can be granted and denied access to this function using the following
	commands:
rexecute()
rexecute()
GRANT REXECUTE ON '<attached_dsn_name>' TO <user_name>
REVOKE REXECUTE ON '<attached_dsn_name>' FROM <user_name>
rstmtexec() provides a short-hand to this function.
rstmtexec()
